terms.note: Tab name: the photo and video library. Also the plural of image in general. Feminine plural. Inside a sentence no article: in Immagini, da Immagini.
Singular in the setup texts: the downloadable system image written to the microSD card, not a photo. Feminine. Say immagine di sistema where it could be read as a photo.
Tab name: the people face recognition found. Also the generic word people, so not enforced.
Tab name. Groups of images are always called collections, in every app and on the site; never albums. As Apple’s Foto app calls its collections.
One group of images. Feminine; plural raccolte.
Action in Images. Other texts quote it, so it is always these exact words.
Tab name: the folders and files on the device. Also the generic plural files. Invariable: il file, i file.
One file. Masculine, invariable.
A folder on the device or on a computer. Feminine; plural cartelle.
Plural of folder.
Tab name: friends’ posts.
Tab name; also the generic plural.
One friend. The person’s gender is unknown: prefer the plural, the person’s name or a neutral wording. Amica for a woman; with {name}, leave the word out.
Tab name: the device’s alerts and friends’ activity. Not the same word as notifications.
Tab name; also the phone’s own Settings app. macOS: Impostazioni di Sistema.
Menu heading above Social and Friends.
The Off The Cloud box (a Raspberry Pi with its disks) that holds everything; also the menu heading Device. Never server, NAS or box in app text. Masculine; plural dispositivi.
Plural of device.

Our relay at off-the.cloud that connects the apps and friends to a device away from home. A common noun, lowercase inside a sentence, one fixed word per language. Masculine, invariable: il bridge, i bridge.
Being reachable through the bridge (a Settings section and the request a user account can carry).
Checkbox label quoted in other texts.
An account: the off-the.cloud account (bridge), a person’s account on the device (Settings, Users), or a Tailscale, Apple or Google account. Masculine, invariable.
Plural of account.
A person with an account on the device. Masculine or feminine: l’utente.
Plural of user; also the Users section in Settings.
The device’s owner: the person who set it up and manages its users.
The device password (it also unlocks the encryption) or an account password. Feminine, invariable: la password.
Plural of password.
One-time code from the off-the.cloud account page that links a new device to the account.
Plural of setup code.
Choice on the setup page and the account page; quoted on the site.
To set up a device the first time. The noun is setup. Noun: configurazione.
Button on the welcome screens; quoted on the site.
Bring a device back from a disk taken out of it (recovery). Noun: recupero.
Setup button; quoted in other texts and on the site.
Setup button next to Recover this device; quoted on the site.
Setup button that makes the device’s light flash; the apps quote it.
Space on the device’s disks; also the Storage line at the foot of the menu. Archiviazione as a short label.
A storage disk or card plugged into the device. Plural dischi.
The two disks kept as copies of each other (RAID 1). RAID itself is never translated. Masculine, invariable; mirrored: in mirror.
Keeping a folder the same in two places. Noun sincronizzazione; synced sincronizzato.
A folder synced in both directions (desktop apps).
A folder copied one way to the device (always upload only), and photo backup from the phones. Masculine, invariable. Verb: fare il backup.
Send a file from a phone or a computer to the device. Noun: caricamento.
Bring a file from the device to a phone or a computer. Noun: download.

A folder option: nothing in the folder can be deleted, and uploading a file again keeps its older version. The name of the option, used as a label and inside sentences. Label Solo caricamento; in a sentence: una cartella in solo caricamento.
Same option written as an adjective (an upload-only folder).
Folder action: its photos and videos are not tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them.
State of a folder after Keep out of Images. Worded without gender agreement on purpose.
Undoes Keep out of Images.

A link that lets anyone who has it download shared files until it expires (made with Share in Images and Files). Worded differently as a noun and as an action, so not enforced. Action: Condividi link.
Settings section listing the share links and galleries.
A web page with copies of shared photos and videos, opened with a link.
Action in Images and Files; quoted in other texts.
A friends-only post in Social. English uses post as a noun and as a verb, so not enforced. Masculine, invariable. Verb: pubblicare.
Plural noun: friends’ posts.
Liking a post or a comment: the button, the count and the alert. English like is also a preposition, so not enforced. Button and count (3 Mi piace). Alert: A {name} piace il tuo post.
A comment on a post (noun and verb). Verb: commentare.
The text written with a post.
A request to become friends, between two devices.
Plural of friend request.
Accept a friend request.
Decline a friend request.
Block a friend.
Setting that finds faces so photos can be searched by person; runs on the device.
Setting that recognises what photos and videos show (a beach, a dog) so they can be searched; the result is tags.
The site’s name for image tagging; the same feature, so the same words.
Words found in a photo (beach, dog), shown as search chips. The tags themselves stay in English: they are search keys.
One tag (noun; to tag is not used in the apps). Feminine.
Settings action that runs tagging and face detection again on the whole library.

A file the device stopped processing because processing it kept failing (alert: <name> was set aside). Put the word file before the name so the participle agrees with it. Il file {name} è stato messo da parte.
Settings button that restarts the device.
A software update of the device or an app (noun and verb). Verb: aggiornare.
An update the device should install soon.
Nothing to update.
Start a session with a password or with Apple or Google (web app, account page, setup). Button: Accedi.
End the session in this browser (web app). Button: Esci.
Phones: forget this device on this phone (connection and cache removed). Same words as sign out.
Mac and Windows/Linux apps: stop syncing with this device and remove its folders from the app. Button: Disconnetti.
Wireless network.
Older spelling in the setup page; same as Wi-Fi.
The network at home, where the apps connect straight to the device.
The network the device is on (addresses like 192.168.…).
The phone’s cellular data. Apple says dati cellulare.
The Wi-Fi network the device opens during setup (named Off The Cloud).
The device’s address: a name under off-the.cloud or a ws:// address.
A name registered to the off-the.cloud account (name.off-the.cloud).
Push notifications on phones and in the browser.
The device’s log, in Settings, Logs; it can be sent to us for help. Masculine, invariable.
What friends see: name, picture and a line about the user.
The picture on the profile.
All the photos and videos on the device.
Small preview of a photo or video.
A photo. Images is the tab; inside sentences the apps say photos and videos. Feminine, invariable.
A video. Masculine, invariable.
Plural of video.
A phone running the iPhone or Android app.
Plural of phone.
A computer running the Mac or Windows/Linux app.
Plural of computer.
A screen of an app, or the device’s display.
One of our apps: web, iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows/Linux. Feminine: l’app.
The device’s own pages in a browser.
Mac app wording. The Windows/Linux app says this computer; the two apps’ texts are otherwise identical.
Windows/Linux app wording for this Mac.
Files are encrypted at rest with a key only the password unlocks.
An encryption key.
An older version of a file that the device keeps.
Both sides changed the same file; a copy of one version is kept.
The Raspberry Pi’s two blue USB ports; storage alerts say which one (top or bottom) holds the failed disk. La porta USB blu superiore / inferiore.
Action in Files; quoted on the site.
Phone photo-sync button; quoted in its explanation.
Phone photo-sync button; quoted in its explanation.
Logs button that sends the device’s logs to us; quoted elsewhere.
Button quoted in the onboarding texts.
Mac item that opens the app when the user logs in (the tray has the same item). Follows Apple’s Open at Login; check the wording on a Mac in that language.
Site wording: AI search, done on the device.
Site and account page prices.
Button.
Button; permanent removal. Cancella is erase.
Button; takes something out of a list without deleting it.
Button.
Button.
Button that closes a finished screen.
Button that acknowledges a message.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button in a sequence of steps.
Button.
Field placeholder and button.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button.
Button. The sentence Try again. is in the language section. Sentence: Riprova.
Button that postpones a question.
Button that grants a permission.
Switches a setting on (Turn Off: the opposite). Turn Off: Disattiva.
Mac menu item: Quit Off The Cloud.
Sign-in button. Apple and Google publish the localized button titles; use theirs when they differ.
Sign-in button.
macOS settings app.
macOS and iOS settings pane.
iOS and macOS Control Centre.
macOS settings pane where login items are listed. Check the name on a Mac in that language before shipping.
macOS Trash, where the Mac app moves files deleted by a sync.
The Downloads folder.
Apple’s Photos app (not our Images tab).
The macOS menu bar.
